description: Wicker basketry was a widespread and practical craft in ancient societies, using flexible materials such as willow, reed, cane, rushes, or thin branches woven around a simple framework. These lightweight but durable containers were well suited for gathering and transporting fruit, nuts, vegetables, herbs, firewood, and other everyday goods. Because baskets could be made from locally available plant materials with relatively simple tools, they were inexpensive household necessities used by farmers, foragers, merchants, and laborers alike, although few survive archaeologically because organic fibers decay easily.
